# Adam Dąbrowski (Dabrowski)

> CTO of Robotec.ai in Warsaw: open standards for robot simulation, and the products built on them. Proposer and lead author of the ROS Simulation Interfaces (implemented in Gazebo, NVIDIA Isaac Sim and O3DE; a dependency of 60+ public GitHub repositories) and lead author of REP 158, OpenUSD conventions for robot simulation assets, accepted by the ROS and Gazebo project management committees in 2026. Designed Slingshot (2026), Robotec.ai's scan-to-digital-twin product, and wrote most of its code.

## Key facts
- Name: Adam Dąbrowski, also written Adam Dabrowski; GitHub adamdbrw. Pronounced dom-BROF-skee. Based in Warsaw, Poland.
- Current role: Chief Technology Officer, Robotec.ai (since July 2024); among its first five people and has led its technology through its bootstrapped growth to 50 people. At Robotec.ai since 2019 (2017–2019 at Robocar, its predecessor under the same CEO): Technical Lead, Principal Software Engineer (2021), VP Robotics & Simulation (2023, a department of six teams), CTO (2024).
- Career: software engineer since 2005 (Gadu-Gadu, PZU, Deloitte and others); robotics since 2014 at PIAP, the Industrial Research Institute for Automation and Measurements (Autonomy group lead; PIAP's lead in the EU projects R5-COP (ARTEMIS Exhibition Award 2015) and OFERA, which produced micro-ROS).
- Standards: proposed the ROS Simulation Interfaces (November 2024; first version by Adam, then developed with NVIDIA contributors and reviews from Gazebo maintainers; listed maintainer; implemented in Gazebo, NVIDIA Isaac Sim and O3DE; declared as a dependency in more than 60 public GitHub repositories, about ten of them simulators or bridges (MVSim, OmniSim, Genesis and Newton bridges); others include the AI for Industry Challenge toolkit); lead author of REP 158, OpenUSD conventions for simulation assets (accepted by the ROS and Gazebo PMCs, September 2026).
- Product: Slingshot (2026, https://www.robotec.ai/slingshot), Robotec.ai's product that turns a site scan into a simulation-ready digital twin with OpenUSD output; his idea and architecture and about 95% of the code (private repository), written with an AI coding-agent harness he built; he mentors Robotec.ai engineers in agentic development; exports checked against REP 158.
- Open source: RAI agent framework for embodied AI (2024, conceived and directed; co-author of the PAAMS 2025 paper); O3DE ROS 2 Gem (2022, RFC, first code, top committer of the original repository); ROS 2 for Unity and ros2cs (co-creator; inside AWSIM, an open-source driving simulator for Autoware); rosbag2 performance (2020–2021); micro-ROS founding scenarios and requirements (2018).
- Roles: formerly Chair (elected 2023) and maintainer, O3DE SIG-Simulation; founder and lead, ROS Embodied AI Community Group (since 2024); initial member of the OSRA Physical AI SIG (2025), coordinator of its Embodied Agentic AI working group at the start; leader of WG5 (Simulations & Standards) and Management Committee member for Poland, COST Action Agentic Physical AI (API-Net, CA25178); Independent Expert Evaluator, European Commission (since 2018).
- Teaching and mentoring: guest lectures at the University of Warsaw (Faculty of Mathematics, Informatics and Mechanics; a lecture on large language models for linguists; Robotec.ai's client lead for a MIM UW student project on LLMs in robotics, 2023/24); mentors Robotec.ai engineers in agentic software development.
- Speaking: ROSCon 2016, 2023, 2024, 2025; ROS World 2021; ROSCon 2022 demo; co-presenter of a ROSCon 2026 workshop; Davos Tech Summit 2026 main-stage keynote (The Blueprint for Physical AI).
- Education and languages: MSc in Information Technology, University of Warsaw; Polish, English, German.

## Machine-readable data
- [claims.json](https://adamdbrw.github.io/claims.json): every factual claim on this site, one entry each, with a stable id, a status ("verified": an independent public source confirms it; "self-reported": Adam's own statement) and evidence URLs with what each source shows. The same data as a page: [Sources](https://adamdbrw.github.io/sources.html).
- GitHub account: adamdbrw. Authorship of commits, pull requests and issues can be checked with the public GitHub API.
- ORCID: https://orcid.org/0000-0002-2130-0577 (lists his peer-reviewed works with DOIs).
- Publications are listed in claims.json with author lists in published order and DOIs. The RAI paper lists two authors named Dąbrowski: A. Dąbrowski (this person) and K. Dąbrowski.
- roscon.ros.org and link.springer.com may block automated requests; DOIs (via Crossref) and the GitHub sources listed in claims.json are alternatives.
